docs.title: X-FUSE
docs.text:
Physics-Guided Foundation-Model Feature Fusion & Uncertainty-Aware Segmentation for Correlative Materials Imaging

Across electron, X-ray, and neutron characterization, experimentalists face a fundamental trade-off between spatial resolution and chemical or crystallographic specificity:

  • High-resolution structural modalities (\(I_{\text{HR}}\)) — such as synchrotron XCT, SEM-BSE, BF-TEM / HAADF-STEM, and white-beam neutron radiography — capture sharp nanoscale-to-microscale morphology rapidly, but suffer from overlapping attenuation or atomic-number contrast.
  • Coarse or sparse physical guide modalities (\(G_{\text{LR}}\)) — such as XRD-CT, SEM/STEM-EDS, EELS, EBSD, and time-of-flight Bragg-edge imaging — resolve exact elemental or phase identity, but are \(4\times\text{–}32\times\) coarser or restricted to a handful of sparse 2D slices due to interaction-volume blur, dose limits, or photon/neutron flux.

X-FUSE bridges these modalities in a pure-PyTorch package with zero custom C++/CUDA compilation or vendored sub-repositories (pretrained DINOv2/ViT weights are resolved reproducibly via timm and cached locally, or bypassed offline with pretrained=False). It extracts dense, multi-scale sub-patch Vision Transformer features from \(I_{\text{HR}}\), fits a physics-informed fusion head against \(G_{\text{LR}}\) through a differentiable forward point-spread-function (PSF) operator and sub-pixel drift aligner, and outputs prior-matched super-resolved phase segmentations paired with pixel/voxel-level certainty maps and optional Split Conformal prediction sets.

docs.title: Core Capabilities
docs.text:
1. 3-Line High-Level API (XFuse.fit_predict): Automatic structural normalization, spatial padding/cropping, content-hashed frozen TTA feature caching, Spin-2 CrossAttentionFeatureUpsampler + SpatialConvMLPHead, ApositionalFeatureDebiaser, and Split Conformal RAPS/APS/LAC calibration in three lines of Python.
  2. Quantitative Forward Physics, Porous-Media Void Clamping & 3D Spectral Cubes: Train directly via forward_psf_poisson, compositional_kl, or forward_psf_bce with Gaussian / Moffat / Core+Halo PSFs, Fresnel-fringe-guarded structural void clamping (pore_mask="auto_otsu_fringe_guarded"), and raw 3D (E, H_lr, W_lr) spectral cube unmixing (spectral_unmix=True).
  3. Megapixel Tiling, Out-of-Core Synchrotron Streaming & Differentiable Registration: Hann-windowed 2D overlapping tile inference (tile_size=...), out-of-core Savu HDF5 / DAWN NeXus / Zarr streaming (load_xct_subvolume, load_diad_xrdct, VolumeSliceAccessor), axial depth-PSF 3D deconvolution, and sub-pixel translation / rigid / affine / bspline registration.
  4. Tri-Part Certainty & 1D Voronoi Active Beamtime Steering: Separate chemical entropy, online Welford TTA / tri-plane epistemic variance, and forward physical PSF residual, and schedule optimal sparse \(z\)-slices (suggest_next_slices) or 2D re-scan windows (suggest_2d_rois).
  5. Standardized Scientific I/O & OpenImpala Export: Export and reload uncertainty reports as OME-TIFF (.ome.tif), HDF5/NeXus (.h5), Zarr (.zarr), or NumPy (.npz), generate OpenImpala AMReX multi-phase geometries + conformal bounds (export_for_openimpala), and read vendor .emd, .dm3/.dm4, .bcf, and .hspy archives (x-fuse[io]).

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Using uv (recommended):

git clone https://github.com/BASE-Laboratory/X-FUSE.git
cd X-FUSE

# Install core package + microscopy I/O + developer & docs extras (CPU)
uv sync --extra cpu --extra io --extra dev --extra docs \
  --index-strategy unsafe-best-match \
  --extra-index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu

# Or on a Linux CUDA workstation:
uv sync --extra cuda --extra io --extra dev

Or with pip:

pip install -e ".[io,dev]"

docs.title: 3-Line Quickstart
docs.text:
from x_fuse import XFuse, generate_correlative_phantom_2d, save_uncertainty_report

phantom = generate_correlative_phantom_2d(size=128, downsample_factor=8)
model = XFuse(
    backbone="dinov2_vits14",
    interpolation_mode="cross_attn",
    fusion_method="spatial_mlp",
    loss_fn="forward_psf_bce",
    layers="multiscale",
    align_guide="translation",
    learn_psf=True,
)
report = model.fit_predict(phantom.hr_image, phantom.coarse_guide, epochs=25)

save_uncertainty_report(report, "fused_output.ome.tif", pixel_size_um=0.05)

Continue to Mathematical Theory for the forward-physics and uncertainty formulation, Benchmarks & Regimes for empirical operating regimes, Modality Recipes for domain-specific configurations, or Tutorials & CLI for batch workflows.

docs.title: x_fuse.fusion
docs.text:
Compositional physics-guided foundation-model feature fusion engine CorrelativeFuser (aliased as XFuse).

v1.0 Compositional Architecture: - self.backbone (HighResBackbone): Frozen ViT feature extractor with optional ApositionalFeatureDebiaser and CrossAttentionFeatureUpsampler (interpolation_mode="cross_attn") or JointBilateralUpsampler ("jbu"). - self.head (LinearProbeHead | SpatialConvMLPHead or WindowedGuideCrossAttentionHead): Composable fusion/prediction head coupled to PhysicsForwardModel (supporting Poisson shot-noise deviance NLL, simplex compositional KL, forward-PSF BCE/MSE, and raw 3D spectral/diffraction cube NMF unmixing). - self.guide_aligner (DifferentiableGuideAligner): Translation, rigid, affine, or cubic B-spline deformable scan-distortion registration. - self.calibrator (ConformalCalibrator): Optional finite-sample Split Conformal Prediction calibrator producing (1 - alpha) phase sets.

docs.title: x_fuse.heads
docs.text:
Composable high-resolution fusion and phase-prediction heads for X-FUSE:

  1. LinearProbeHead (aliased as LearnedChannelGating): Fast pixel-wise linear projection + channel ranking supervised via PhysicsForwardModel.
  2. SpatialConvMLPHead (fusion_method="spatial_mlp"): Nonlinear bottleneck MLP + 3x3 depthwise-separable spatial context residual + multi-scale HR texture skip connection + optional edge-aware Total Variation regularization.
  3. WindowedGuideCrossAttentionHead (aliased as XRDCrossAttention / SpatialCrossAttention): Memory-safe O(H * W) pooled-key cross-attention replacing the legacy O((H * W)^2) global attention bottleneck so 512x512+ micrographs run in < 80 MB RAM.

docs.title: WindowedGuideCrossAttentionHead
docs.text:
Bases: Module

Memory-safe O(H * W) pooled-key cross-attention head replacing the legacy O((H * W)^2) global attention bottleneck.

Caps the spatial key/value token grid to at most max_kv_grid x max_kv_grid (default 16 x 16 = 256 tokens) via adaptive average pooling and blends the attended semantic tokens with a local 3x3 residual feature skip, running comfortably on 512x512–2048x2048 micrographs in < 80 MB RAM.

docs.title: x_fuse.physics
docs.text:
Quantitative physical forward operators, likelihood losses, and raw 3D spectral/diffraction cube unmixing for correlative materials imaging.

Supports: 1. SpectralUnmixingDictionary: Non-negative endmember spectral/diffraction dictionary S in R_+^(M x E) initialized via deterministic multiplicative NMF and refined end-to-end against raw (E, H_lr, W_lr) data cubes. 2. PhysicsForwardModel: Unified physical forward operator Lambda_LR = tau * D_Sigma(W_phi(P_HR)) @ S + b with: - Exact Poisson shot-noise deviance negative log-likelihood ("forward_psf_poisson") for low-count EDS, EELS, and fast XRD-CT. - Simplex-constrained compositional phase-fraction conservation ("compositional_kl", guaranteeing sum_k P_k(x) = 1 at every pixel). - Partial-volume "forward_psf_bce", "forward_psf_mse", "bce", and "pearson" objectives.

docs.title: x_fuse.debias
docs.text:
Apositional Vision Transformer feature debiasing to eliminate spatial coordinate-ramp shortcut learning on homogeneous micrographs and macroscopic chemical diffusion gradients.

Motivated by recent findings on ViT positional leakage in electron/X-ray microscopy (e.g., DINO-SAW, Docherty et al., arXiv:2603.16840), frozen DINOv2, DINOv3, MAE, and SAM backbones contain channels that act as smooth (y, x) coordinate ramps. When supervising a probe with a coarse physical map exhibiting a macroscopic spatial gradient (e.g. core-shell catalyst pellet or battery electrode lithiation gradient), an un-debiased probe can overfit to coordinate-ramp channels instead of true grain morphology.

ApositionalFeatureDebiaser removes spatial polynomial ramp components via: 1. Closed-form QR orthonormal spatial polynomial projection (r2_threshold=0.0 projects out (y, x) polynomials across all channels to machine precision; r2_threshold > 0 selectively detrends or attenuates ramp-dominated channels), or 2. Content-free noise/flip calibration (calibrate_from_backbone), identifying intrinsic ViT positional channels on isotropic white noise so genuine sample-level microstructural density gradients remain completely untouched.

docs.title: ApositionalFeatureDebiaser
docs.text:
Bases: Module

Project out spatial coordinate-ramp components from dense or patch-level Vision Transformer features (B, C, H, W).

Modes: - mode="orthogonal" (default): Projects out spatial coordinate polynomials up to degree. When r2_threshold == 0.0, applies exact orthogonal projection across all channels (driving linear/quadratic coordinate R^2 to 0). When r2_threshold > 0.0, only detrends channels whose positional R^2 exceeds r2_threshold (or calibrated noise channels). - mode="attenuate": Scales each channel by (1 - pos_r2) to damp positional channels without altering spatial profiles of content channels.

docs.title: calibrate_on_homogeneous_noise(feature_extractor_fn, image_hw=(224, 224), n_samples=3, r2_cutoff=0.15, device='cpu', seed=0)
docs.text:
Identify intrinsic content-free ViT positional channels by probing feature_extractor_fn with isotropic white-noise images (which contain zero macroscopic spatial gradient). Any channel exhibiting high spatial coordinate R^2 on white noise is an intrinsic ViT positional ramp.

Returns the per-channel intrinsic positional R^2 vector (C,).

docs.title: CrossAttentionFeatureUpsampler
docs.text:
Bases: Module

JAFAR/AnyUp-inspired local HR-query cross-attention upsampler running in O(H * W * K^2) memory without custom CUDA kernels.

Why this improves over classical JointBilateralUpsampler: 1. Queries Q_HR(y, x) combine multi-scale HR structural + local texture energy descriptors (std_3x3, std_7x7, Laplacian) with optional D_4-equivariant spin-2 structure-tensor orientation fields (orientation_aware=True), cleanly separating both textured vs. smooth phases and differently oriented iso-intensity lamellar colonies. 2. When subtoken_offsets=True, performs direct 3 x 3 coarse-token neighborhood cross-attention conditioned on continuous sub-token coordinate offsets Delta_{pq} before fine HR boundary snapping, eliminating 14-16 px bilinear pre-blur across grain boundaries. 3. Works both zero-shot (learned=False) and end-to-end trainable (learned=True) under the physical forward-PSF loss.

docs.title: x_fuse.uncertainty
docs.text:
Pixel- and voxel-level uncertainty quantification, calibration, physical forward-model consistency diagnostics, and finite-sample Split Conformal Prediction sets for correlative materials fusion.

Provides four complementary uncertainty & statistical guarantee mechanisms: 1. Aleatoric / Chemical Ambiguity: Calibrated class/element posterior entropy and top-1 vs. top-2 probability margin. 2. Epistemic / Spatial & Volumetric Variance: Online Welford variance across TTA shift/flip transforms and 2.5D orthogonal tri-plane views (zero extra ViT storage overhead), plus BALD mutual information. 3. Physical Forward-Model Residual: Discrepancy |D(P_HR) - G_LR| between PSF-downsampled high-resolution predictions and the measured coarse physical guide—flagging regions where the structural modality lacks contrast for a chemical gradient. 4. Split Conformal Prediction (ConformalCalibrator): Distribution-free (1 - alpha) phase prediction sets C_{1-alpha}(x) and locally adaptive coarse physical error bounds calibrated on held-out spatial blocks or labels.

Aggregate a dictionary of {q: map_2d} Bragg reflection maps into a single 2D phase intensity map.

  • "all_sum" / "all_mean": Sums or averages all fitted reflections for maximum SNR and reduced overlapping-doublet crosstalk.
  • "positive_sum": Clamps negative background baseline excursions before summing.

docs.title: Benchmarks & Operating Regimes
docs.text: X-FUSE is evaluated across both synthetic controlled-physics stress tests and real open-access correlative synchrotron, STEM, and SEM datasets. A central principle of X-FUSE is honest operating-regime characterization: foundation-model feature fusion is not a silver bullet for every micrograph, and knowing when classical edge-guided filtering suffices—or when structural contrast is physically absent—is essential for trustworthy scientific deployment.

docs.title: 1. Formal Operating Regime Taxonomy
docs.text: Regime Structural vs. Chemical Relationship Representative Materials Examples Recommended Method Quantitative Behavior Regime A — Contrast-Complete Piecewise-Smooth Distinct phases exhibit clean, monotonic 1D intensity separation in \(I_{\text{HR}}\) (SNR > 10) High-\(Z\) intermetallics vs. pores/matrix in BSE or attenuation XCT Classical Multi-Otsu or JBU (or XFuse when conformal UQ / drift alignment is needed) Otsu, Guided TV, and X-FUSE all reach >0.97 mIoU (4×–8×); classical filters run in <0.1s Regime B1 — Iso-Intensity Multi-Scale / Oriented Texture Distinct chemical phases share identical mean grayscale intensity (\(\Delta\mu \approx 0\)) and pixel variance, differing only in sub-PSF spatial morphology or lamellar orientation Pearlitic / \(\alpha+\beta\) Ti lamellar colonies, oriented eutectic precipitates, spinodal textures X-FUSE (cross_attn + spatial_mlp) At 16× Moffat blur, X-FUSE achieves 0.8908 mIoU (0.9317 BF1) vs. 0.7276 Guided TV (+16.3 pp), 0.6662 SIREN INR (+22.5 pp), 0.6186 JBU (+27.2 pp), and 0.3342 Otsu (+55.7 pp) Regime B2 — Heavy-Tailed Probe / Axial 3D Blur & Drift Sharp \(I_{\text{HR}}\) paired with Lorentzian/Moffat synchrotron wings, SEM backscattered core_halo skirts, sub-pixel stage drift, or thick axial 3D interaction volumes Synchrotron XRD-CT (Zn13X), 15–20 kV SEM-EDS (edxia LC3), sparse-slice 3D tomography X-FUSE (psf_profile="moffat" | "core_halo", learn_psf=True, align_guide=..., VolumetricFuser) +8.8 pp mIoU from core_halo PSF modeling; +19.1 pp mIoU from differentiable drift alignment at 4 px shift; +6.8 pp 3D mIoU from learnable axial depth-PSF deconvolution Regime C — Contrast-Incomplete / Invisible Zonation Chemical variation or crystallographic polymorph transition produces zero contrast (\(\Delta\mu = 0\), \(\Delta\text{texture} = 0\)) in \(I_{\text{HR}}\) Macroscopic solid-solution diffusion profiles, polymorphs with identical mass attenuation X-FUSE (guide_residual=True, debias_positional=True, ConformalCalibrator) Smooth coarse chemical zonation is preserved via guide_residual=True without ViT positional ramp artifacts (R^2 -> 0.0), while physical_residual and RAPS prediction sets widen to flag unresolved sub-PSF boundaries

Using the open Diamond Light Source K11 DIAD Zn-13X dataset (10.5281/zenodo.13329639), benchmarks/run_zn13x_multiscale_couplings.py validates X-FUSE across real dual-beamsize synchrotron hardware and porous-media simulation handoff:

  • Real Dual-Beamsize 50 µm → 25 µm Hardware Audit (4 Paired Axial Slices): Correcting the +47.5° gts_cs_theta soft-motor zero offset on 50 µm scans (43345→43324, 43395→43322, 43398→43323, 43399→43325) and aggregating all fitted Bragg reflections lifts cross-resolution \(f_{ ext{Zn}}\) Pearson \(r\) from 0.3417 (MAE = 0.1818, legacy single-peak 0°) \( ightarrow\) 0.8678 (+47.5° fix) \( ightarrow\) 0.9291 (all_sum + +47.5°) \( ightarrow\) 0.9343 (positive_sum + +47.5°, MAE = 0.0387, +59.3 pp).
  • Chemical VoDaSuRe Synthetic-vs.-Real Domain Gap: Synthetic 2× Moffat downsampling of the 25 µm XRD-CT scans yields mean \(r = \mathbf{0.9810}\), whereas real 50 µm dual-beamsize hardware yields \(r = \mathbf{0.9343}\) — quantifying a real synchrotron hardware gap of \(\Delta r = 0.0468\) (peaking at 0.1124 on low-Zn reaction-tail slice 43398→43323).
  • Synchrotron XCT Artifact Cleanup, Fringe-Guarded pore_mask, & OpenImpala Export: Combining detrend_radial_cupping (for segmentation thresholding only), remove_polar_rings_conservative, and Fourier Tie-homogeneity phase-fringe damping (pore_mask="auto_otsu_fringe_guarded") improves corrupted pore-mask IoU (0.6567 → 0.7018), enforces 0.0 void chemical leakage inside detected pores, and exports uncompressed uint8 3D multi-phase TIFFs + (1-\alpha) conformal lower/upper phase-envelope geometries + AMReX ParmParse .inputs decks via export_for_openimpala.
  • MultimodalBenchmark Band-Limited Task T3 (k <= 0.43 cyc/px, ~58 µm) & Two-Track Cupping Audit: Under raised-cosine Fourier band-limiting to the 25 µm XRD-CT SB-FRC cutoff (0.43 cyc/px), X-FUSE (v1.0.0) achieves reduced \(\chi^2_ u = \mathbf{0.9287}\) (at the 1.0 diffraction noise floor) and band-limited RMSE = 0.3619 (r = 0.9965) vs. CNMF (\(\chi^2_ u = 5.07\), RMSE = 0.8581), Bicubic (\(\chi^2_ u = 13.78\), RMSE = 1.4085), Guided-TV (\(\chi^2_ u = 23.41\)), and JBU (\(\chi^2_ u = 25.43\)), while confirming that 7-term radial cupping subtraction is strongly confounded with core–shell Zn chemistry (\(r(\Delta_{ ext{cup}}, ext{Zn}) = +0.5493\)) whereas conservative polar de-ringing preserves radial chemical contrast (\(r = -0.0857\)).

docs.title: Modality Recipes
docs.text: X-FUSE uses a single modality-neutral interface across X-ray, electron, and neutron characterization. Below are recommended parameter recipes for common laboratory and beamline setups.

docs.title: 1. Synchrotron XCT + XRD-CT (2D & Sparse-Slice 2.5D)
docs.text:
• Physical Regime: High-resolution attenuation/phase-contrast XCT (\(I_{\text{HR}}\), \(0.5\text{–}2\,\mu\text{m}\) voxel) paired with pencil-beam XRD-CT (\(G_{\text{LR}}\), \(5\times\text{–}20\times\) coarser in-plane or acquired on only \(3\text{–}25\) sparse \(z\)-slices).
  • Recommended Setup:
  • Enable VolumetricFuser with delta=1 (2.5d_slab, 3-slice [z-1, z, z+1] context) for training on sparse XRD-CT slices and mode="triplane" for full-volume 3D propagation.
  • Stream large HDF5/NeXus or Zarr reconstructions lazily without loading the entire 3D tomogram into RAM.
import h5py
from x_fuse import XFuse, VolumetricFuser, export_for_openimpala, suggest_next_slices

base = XFuse(
    backbone="dinov2_vits14",
    layers="multiscale",
    stride=4,
    pore_mask="auto_otsu_fringe_guarded",
    conformal_alpha=0.10,
    conformal_method="raps",
)
vol_fuser = VolumetricFuser(base)

with h5py.File("xct_tomogram.h5", "r") as hf:
    xct_lazy = hf["entry/reconstruction/data"]  # Streamed slice-by-slice!
    vol_fuser.fit_sparse_slices(
        xct_lazy,
        sparse_guides={10: xrd_z10, 50: xrd_z50},
        epochs=20,
        pore_mask="auto_otsu_fringe_guarded",
        depth_psf_sigma=1.8,
        learn_depth_psf=True,
        triplane_consistency_weight=0.15,
    )
    vol_report = vol_fuser.predict_volume(
        xct_lazy,
        mode="triplane",
        sparse_guides={10: xrd_z10, 50: xrd_z50},
        pred_mode="multiclass",
        pore_mask="auto_otsu_fringe_guarded",
    )

# Export multi-phase uint8 geometry + conformal envelopes for OpenImpala AMReX PDE transport:
export_for_openimpala(vol_report, "./openimpala_geom", name="zeolite_pellet", active_phase=0)

# Recommend the next 3 XRD-CT z-slices to scan during live beamtime (1D Voronoi steering):
plan = suggest_next_slices(vol_report, acquired_indices=[10, 50], k=3, min_spacing=8)
print("Next XRD-CT slices:", plan.recommended_indices)

docs.title: 2. SEM-BSE + Multi-Element EDS / EBSD
docs.text:
• Physical Regime: Backscattered electron micrograph (\(I_{\text{HR}}\), \(5\text{–}20\,\text{nm}\) pixel) paired with \(15\text{–}20\,\text{kV}\) EDS elemental maps (\(G_{\text{LR}}\), \(\sim 1\text{–}2\,\mu\text{m}\) pear-shaped interaction volume) where a narrow primary beam core is surrounded by a wide backscattered X-ray excitation skirt, and higher-energy lines (e.g., Fe-K\(\alpha\), Ca-K\(\alpha\)) excite wider volumes than low-energy lines (Mg-K\(\alpha\), Si-K\(\alpha\)).
  • Recommended Setup:
  • Set psf_profile="core_halo" and learn_psf=True so ForwardPSFDownsampler models both the narrow primary beam core and wide backscattered excitation halo per element.
  • Set loss_fn="compositional_kl" with guide_residual=True when fusing calibrated wt%/at% EDS maps on the simplex.
  • Set tile_size=512 for large-area stitched SEM mosaics (\(2048^2\text{–}8192^2\)).
from x_fuse import XFuse

model = XFuse(
    backbone="dinov2_vitb14_reg",
    interpolation_mode="cross_attn",
    fusion_method="spatial_mlp",
    layers="multiscale",
    loss_fn="compositional_kl",
    psf_profile="core_halo",
    learn_psf=True,
    guide_residual=True,
    align_guide="translation",
    tile_size=512,
    tile_overlap=64,
)
report = model.fit_predict(bse_mosaic, eds_element_stack, epochs=30, mode="multiclass")
print("Learned per-element PSF sigmas:", report.diagnostics["psf_sigma_yx_hr_px"])

docs.title: 3. HAADF-STEM + Dose-Limited STEM-EDS / Core-Loss EELS
docs.text:
• Physical Regime: Rapid, low-dose HAADF survey image (\(I_{\text{HR}}\)) paired with a coarse-step STEM-EDS or 3D core-loss EELS spectrum image (\(G_{\text{LR}}\)) susceptible to sample stage drift and small nanoscale fields of view (<112 px).
  • Recommended Setup:
  • Load .emd, .dm4, or .hspy vendor files directly via load_microscopy_file (pip install x-fuse[io]).
  • For raw 3D (E, H_lr, W_lr) EELS/EDS cubes, enable loss_fn="forward_psf_poisson", spectral_unmix=True, and guide_residual=True; min_input_size="auto" automatically bicubic-upscales small nanoscale survey crops before ViT extraction to prevent token starvation.
  • Set align_guide="rigid" or "translation" to compensate sub-pixel specimen drift, and run suggest_2d_rois to target high-uncertainty precipitates for fine-step EELS re-acquisition.
from x_fuse import XFuse, load_microscopy_file, suggest_2d_rois

haadf, _ = load_microscopy_file("survey_haadf.dm4")
ti_map, _ = load_microscopy_file("eds_Ti.emd")
mo_map, _ = load_microscopy_file("eds_Mo.emd")

model = XFuse(
    backbone="dinov2_vits14",
    interpolation_mode="cross_attn",
    fusion_method="spatial_mlp",
    loss_fn="forward_psf_bce",
    align_guide="rigid",
    psf_profile="moffat",
    learn_psf=True,
    guide_residual=True,
    conformal_alpha=0.10,
    conformal_method="raps",
)
report = model.fit_predict(haadf, [ti_map, mo_map], epochs=25)

rois = suggest_2d_rois(report, roi_size=(64, 64), k=3)

docs.title: 4. White-Beam Neutron Imaging + ToF Bragg-Edge Mapping
docs.text:
• Physical Regime: High-flux white-beam neutron attenuation radiograph/tomogram (\(I_{\text{HR}}\)) fused with wavelength-resolved Time-of-Flight (ToF) Bragg-edge phase fraction or strain maps (\(G_{\text{LR}}\), e.g., fcc/bcc Iron phase transformation or multi-metal powder phantoms).
  • Recommended Setup:
  • Pay special attention to report.physical_residual and report.unresolved_mask: crystallographic texture or phase transitions (such as martensitic vs. austenitic steel) can have nearly identical white-beam attenuation in \(I_{\text{HR}}\), which X-FUSE's forward-PSF residual explicitly flags rather than hallucinating false sharp boundaries.

docs.title: Mathematical Theory
docs.text: X-FUSE formulates correlative super-resolution segmentation as physically constrained inverse inference conditioned on dense self-supervised structural features.

docs.title: 1. Dense Sub-Patch Multi-Layer ViT Feature Extraction
docs.text:
Given a structural micrograph \(I_{\text{HR}} \in \mathbb{R}^{H \times W}\), X-FUSE modifies the patch-embedding convolution stride of a pretrained Vision Transformer (DINOv2, DINOv3, ALiBi, NoPE, or timm ViT) from patch size \(p\) (typically \(14\) or \(16\)) down to sub-patch stride \(s \in \{2, 4, 7, 8\}\) while interpolating positional embeddings accordingly.

When layers="multiscale" is enabled, patch tokens are extracted across shallow, mid-level, and deep transformer blocks \(\ell \in \mathcal{L}\) (e.g. quarter, half, three-quarter, and final depth), each individually LayerNorm-stabilized and channel-concatenated:

\[ F_{\text{raw}}(x) = \bigoplus_{\ell \in \mathcal{L}} \mathrm{LN}\!\left(T^{(\ell)}(x)\right) \in \mathbb{R}^{(\sum_\ell D_\ell) \times H_f \times W_f} \]

Shallow ViT blocks preserve sharp high-frequency pore, grain, and precipitate edges, while deeper blocks capture multi-grain textural context.

docs.title: Feature Upsampling: Scale-Dilated JBU & Texture-Aware Cross-Attention
docs.text:
Rather than nearest-neighbor or bilinear upsampling from the stride-\(s\) token grid \((H_f, W_f)\) to \((H, W)\), X-FUSE provides two complementary high-resolution feature upsamplers:

  1. Scale-Dilated Joint Bilateral Upsampling (interpolation_mode="jbu"): Pure-PyTorch progressive bilateral filtering conditioned on normalized structural intensity \(g = I_{\text{HR}}\): $$ w_{\text{JBU}}(p, q) = \exp!\left(-\frac{|p - q|_2^2}{2\sigma_s^2}\right) \exp!\left(-\frac{|g(p) - g(q)|_2^2}{2\sigma_r^2}\right) $$
  2. Spin-2 Orientation-Aware & Continuous Sub-Token Cross-Attention (interpolation_mode="cross_attn", CrossAttentionFeatureUpsampler): Inspired by continuous coordinate-query upsamplers (JAFAR / AnyUp), each pixel \(p \in \{1, \dots, H\} \times \{1, \dots, W\}\) extracts an 8-channel multiscale texture descriptor \(\tau(p)\) augmented—when orientation_aware=True—by a 4-channel multiscale spin-2 structure-tensor director field \(\mathbf{s}(p) = (c_1 \cos 2\theta_1, c_1 \sin 2\theta_1, c_2 \cos 2\theta_2, c_2 \sin 2\theta_2)\) derived from smoothed outer products \(J_\sigma = G_\sigma * (\nabla I_{\text{HR}} \nabla I_{\text{HR}}^\top)\) with local coherence \(c = \frac{\lambda_1 - \lambda_2}{\lambda_1 + \lambda_2 + \epsilon}\). Because grain boundaries and lamellae carry headless orientation (\(\theta \equiv \theta + \pi\)), encoding \(2\theta\) makes \(\theta\) and \(\theta + \pi\) identical while orthogonal colonies (\(\theta + \pi/2\)) negate both spin-2 components (\(\cos 2(\theta + \pi/2) = -\cos 2\theta\)), cleanly separating differently oriented iso-intensity colonies! When subtoken_offsets=True, continuous sub-token offsets \(\Delta_{pq} = (\Delta y_{pq}, \Delta x_{pq}) \in [-1.5, 1.5]^2\) enter both via isotropic radial decay and an exact \(D_4\)-equivariant learned bilinear distance penalty.

docs.title: Apositional Feature Debiasing (debias_positional=True)
docs.text: Pretrained Vision Transformers with learned absolute positional embeddings or RoPE encode linear and quadratic \((y, x)\) coordinate ramps in dedicated feature channels (dino-saw, Docherty et al., 2026). On materials exhibiting macroscopic chemical gradients (diffusion couples, battery electrodes, thermal-barrier coatings), a probe can overfit to image coordinates \((y, x)\) instead of microstructure. ApositionalFeatureDebiaser projects each feature channel onto the orthogonal complement of normalized degree-\(d\) bivariate Legendre polynomials \(\mathcal{B}_d(y, x)\), driving coordinate \(R^2 \to 0\) on any standard ViT without custom re-pretraining.

docs.title: 2. Quantitative Forward Physics, Heavy-Tailed PSFs & B-Spline Registration
docs.text:
Naive correlative fusion upsamples the coarse chemical guide \(G_{\text{LR}}\) to \((H, W)\) and trains against blurry targets—actively penalizing crisp high-resolution phase boundaries.

Instead, X-FUSE predicts high-resolution phase abundances \(\hat{P}_{\text{HR}} \in [0, 1]^{M \times H \times W}\) via a LinearProbeHead, nonlinear SpatialConvMLPHead (fusion_method="spatial_mlp"), or \(O(HW)\) WindowedGuideCrossAttentionHead (fusion_method="attention"), warps them into the guide frame via \(\mathcal{W}_\theta\) (DifferentiableGuideAligner), and applies an anisotropic forward PSF operator \(\mathcal{D}_\Sigma\) (ForwardPSFDownsampler):

\[ \hat{G}_{\text{LR}} = \mathcal{D}_\Sigma\!\left(\mathcal{W}_\theta(\hat{P}_{\text{HR}})\right) = \mathrm{AvgPool}_{r_y, r_x}\!\left(K_{\Sigma}^{(m)} * \mathcal{W}_\theta(\hat{P}_{\text{HR}})_m\right) \]

To match real electron, X-ray, and neutron microprobes without Gaussian inverse crime, ForwardPSFDownsampler supports three learnable per-channel PSF families (psf_profile):

  • "gaussian": Separable anisotropic Gaussian \(K_{\sigma_y, \sigma_x}(\Delta y, \Delta x) \propto \exp\!\left(-\frac{\Delta y^2}{2\sigma_y^2} - \frac{\Delta x^2}{2\sigma_x^2}\right)\).
  • "moffat": Non-separable heavy-tailed Lorentzian/Moffat probe skirt \(K_{\alpha_y, \alpha_x, \beta}(\Delta y, \Delta x) \propto \left(1 + \frac{\Delta y^2}{\alpha_y^2} + \frac{\Delta x^2}{\alpha_x^2}\right)^{-\beta}\) with learnable tail index \(\beta > 1.05\).
  • "core_halo": Double-Gaussian primary beam core plus secondary fluorescence / Monte Carlo backscattered interaction halo \((1 - w_h) K_{\sigma_y, \sigma_x}^{\text{core}} + w_h K_{\eta \sigma_y, \eta \sigma_x}^{\text{halo}}\) with learnable halo fraction \(w_h \in (0, 0.5)\) and width ratio \(\eta > 1\).

PhysicsForwardModel pairs these forward operators with quantitative counting-statistics objectives:

  • Poisson Shot-Noise Deviance (loss_fn="forward_psf_poisson"): Exact maximum-likelihood negative log-likelihood for low-dose STEM-EDS, EELS, XRF, and time-of-flight Bragg-edge photon/neutron counts \(C_{\text{LR}} \sim \mathrm{Poisson}(s_m \hat{G}_{\text{LR}, m} + b_m)\) with learnable per-channel gain \(s_m > 0\) and background \(b_m \ge 0\): $$ \mathcal{L}{\text{Poisson}}(\hat{\Lambda}, C) = 2 \sum{m, u} \left[\hat{\Lambda}{m,u} - C{m,u} + C_{m,u} \log!\left(\frac{\max(C_{m,u}, \epsilon)}{\hat{\Lambda}_{m,u}}\right)\right] $$
  • Simplex Mass/Atomic-Fraction Conservation (loss_fn="compositional_kl"): Enforces \(\hat{P}_{\text{HR}} = \mathrm{softmax}(Z_{\text{HR}}) \in \Delta^{K-1}\) (\(\sum_{k=1}^K \hat{P}_{k}(x) = 1\) at every pixel) supervised via forward-PSF Kullback–Leibler divergence.
  • 3D Spectral / Diffraction Cube Unmixing (SpectralUnmixingDictionary, spectral_unmix=True): Accepts raw \((E, H_{\text{LR}}, W_{\text{LR}})\) EDS/EELS/XRD cubes directly without external pre-fitting, jointly learning non-negative endmember spectra \(S \in \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}^{M \times E}\) (\(\sum_e S_{m,e} = 1\), initialized via Successive Projection Algorithm + multiplicative NMF) alongside super-resolved spatial abundances: \(\hat{Y}_{e, u} = \sum_{m=1}^M \alpha_m \hat{G}_{\text{LR}, m, u} S_{m, e} + b_e\).
  • Cubic B-Spline Non-Rigid Registration (align_guide="bspline"): Compensates nonlinear SEM/STEM charging drift and scan-coil hysteresis via a bicubic control-point displacement field regularized by thin-plate bending energy \(\|\nabla^2 u\|_2^2\) and monitored via minimum Jacobian determinant \(\min \det J_{\mathcal{W}}\) for diffeomorphic invertibility.
  • Fringe-Guarded Porous-Media Void Clamping (pore_mask="auto_otsu_fringe_guarded"): In porous catalysts and electrodes, structural voids (\(M_{\text{pore}} = 1\)) contain zero solid phase while coarse diffraction/EDS voxels suffer partial-volume pore dilution. segment_pores_otsu damps 1–2 px Fresnel propagation phase-contrast overshoots solely during threshold estimation via a Fourier Tie-homogeneity filter \(\mathcal{F}^{-1}\{\mathcal{F}(I_{\text{HR}}) / (1 + \alpha \|\mathbf{k}\|_2^2)\}\) (without blurring \(I_{\text{HR}}\)) and clamps void logits prior to \(\mathcal{D}_\Sigma\), deconvolving solid-framework stoichiometry with zero void leakage.

docs.title: 3. Prior Calibration, Tri-Part Uncertainty & Split Conformal Sets
docs.text:
After fitting, X-FUSE calibrates high-resolution posteriors via match_coarse_priors so spatial means match physical coarse phase fractions, and decomposes pixel/voxel uncertainty into:

  1. Aleatoric / Chemical Ambiguity (\(U_{\text{alea}}\)): Normalized Shannon entropy \(-\frac{1}{\log K} \sum_{k=1}^{K} p_k(x) \log p_k(x) \in [0, 1]\).
  2. Epistemic / View Disagreement (\(U_{\text{epi}}\)): Computed in \(O(1)\) auxiliary memory via an online Welford accumulator across invertible sub-patch TTA views (and orthogonal XY, XZ, YZ planes in 2.5D mode).
  3. Physical Forward-Model Residual (\(U_{\text{phys}}\)): Upsampled \(|\mathcal{D}_\Sigma(\mathcal{W}_\theta(\hat{P}_{\text{HR}})) - G_{\text{LR}}|\), automatically flagging structurally invisible phases carrying zero contrast in \(I_{\text{HR}}\).

docs.title: Temperature-Scaled Regularized Adaptive Conformal Prediction (ConformalCalibrator)
docs.text:
When conformal_alpha \(\alpha \in (0, 1)\) is specified (or calibrated against sparse reference labels via ConformalCalibrator.calibrate_labels), X-FUSE supports Least Ambiguous Set-Valued Classifiers ("lac"), Adaptive Prediction Sets ("aps"), and Regularized Adaptive Prediction Sets ("raps", Angelopoulos et al., ICLR 2021) with post-hoc NLL temperature scaling (fit_temperature=True) on spatially disjoint checkerboard blocks (spatial_block_size \(b\)):

\[ s_{\text{RAPS}}(x, y) = \sum_{j=1}^{r(x, y) - 1} \tilde{\pi}_{(j)}(x; T) + u \cdot \tilde{\pi}_{(r(x, y))}(x; T) + \lambda_{\text{reg}} \max\!\left(0,\, r(x, y) - k_{\text{reg}}\right) \]

where \(\tilde{\pi}(x; T) = \mathrm{softmax}(\log p(x) / T)\) is fit on half of the \(b \times b\) spatial blocks and the conformal quantile \(\hat{q}_{1-\alpha}\) is evaluated at finite-sample effective sample size \(N_{\text{eff}} = \lfloor N_{\text{cal}} / b^2 \rfloor\) on the complementary blocks. This yields compact singleton sets inside homogeneous grain interiors while expanding cleanly to 2-phase sets along diffuse interphase boundaries.

docs.title: 4. 1D Voronoi-Integrated Active Sparse-Slice & ROI Steering
docs.text:
During synchrotron or electron-microscopy beamtime, suggest_next_slices ranks candidate unmeasured \(z\)-slices in a 3D tomogram by combining local axial-correlation-discounted uncertainty \(\hat{U}(c \mid \mathcal{S}) = (w_{\text{epi}} \tilde{U}_{\text{epi}}(c) + w_{\text{alea}} \tilde{U}_{\text{alea}}(c))(1 - e^{-d_{\mathcal{S}}(c)/\ell_z})\) with 1D Voronoi distance-reduction integration across the full axial stack:

\[ \mathcal{A}(c \mid \mathcal{S}) = 0.55\, \hat{U}(c \mid \mathcal{S}) + \frac{0.45}{Z_{\max}} \sum_{z=1}^{Z} \left(\hat{U}(z \mid \mathcal{S}) + w_{\text{dist}}\right) \max\!\left(0,\, d_{\mathcal{S}}(z) - |z - c|\right) \]

where \(d_{\mathcal{S}}(z) = \min_{s \in \mathcal{S}} |z - s|\), subject to minimum slice spacing \(\Delta z_{\min}\). This immediately discovers localized reaction fronts on initial scouts while naturally bisecting unvisited bulk intervals as the acquisition budget grows. Similarly, suggest_2d_rois evaluates exact \(O(HW)\) integral-image sliding-window sums over \((1 - w_r) U_{\text{comb}} + w_r U_{\text{phys}}\) with non-maximum suppression to schedule non-overlapping 2D re-acquisition windows.

docs.title: 5. 3D Axial Interaction-Volume Deconvolution & Tri-Plane Consistency
docs.text:
In correlative 3D tomography (VolumetricFuser), a 2D chemical or diffraction map acquired at nominal slice \(z_k\) (e.g., polished FIB-SEM-EDS or thick-beam XRD-CT) integrates signal across an axial interaction depth \(\sigma_z > 0\) rather than an infinitesimally thin plane. When depth_psf_sigma > 0, VolumetricFuser.fit_sparse_slices supervises an axial stencil \(z_k + \delta\) (\(\delta \in \{-R, \dots, R\}\)) weighted by a normalized Gaussian depth kernel \(w_\delta \propto \exp(-\delta^2 / 2\sigma_z^2)\) (optionally learning \(\sigma_z\) jointly via learn_depth_psf=True):

\[ \hat{P}_{\text{slab}}(z_k) = \sum_{\delta=-R}^{R} w_\delta(\sigma_z)\, \hat{P}_{\text{HR}}(z_k + \delta), \qquad \mathcal{L}_{\text{3D}} = \mathcal{L}_{\text{phys}}\!\left(\mathcal{D}_\Sigma(\hat{P}_{\text{slab}}(z_k)),\, G_{\text{LR}}(z_k)\right) + \lambda_{\text{tri}} \mathcal{L}_{\text{JSD}}(P_{XY}, P_{XZ}, P_{YZ}) \]

When triplane_consistency_weight \(\lambda_{\text{tri}} > 0\), randomly sampled unguided interior voxels are regularized via symmetric Jensen–Shannon divergence \(\mathcal{L}_{\text{JSD}}\) across orthogonal XY, XZ, and YZ 2.5D slice predictions, suppressing slice-to-slice striping between sparse chemical acquisitions.

docs.title: Command-Line Interface (xfuse)
docs.text: Installing x-fuse registers the xfuse command-line tool for environment verification, Zenodo dataset discovery, synthetic smoke testing, and zero-code batch correlative fusion.

docs.title: 1. Environment Diagnostics & Open Datasets
docs.text:
# Print JSON runtime summary (Python, PyTorch, CUDA availability)
xfuse info

# List or download registered open-access correlative datasets on Zenodo
xfuse datasets
xfuse datasets --json
xfuse datasets --fetch edxia_cement_sem_eds --dest ./zenodo_cache

docs.title: 2. Self-Contained Synthetic Smoke Benchmark
docs.text: xfuse demo --epochs 15 --output demo_metrics.json

docs.title: 3. Batch 2D & Sparse-Slice 3D Correlative Fusion (xfuse fuse / xfuse fuse-3d)
docs.text:
Fuse a high-resolution 2D structural micrograph (.tif, .png, .npy, .emd, .dm4, .hspy) with one or more coarse physical guide maps and export a calibrated multi-channel report to OME-TIFF, HDF5, or Zarr:

xfuse fuse \
  --hr data/samples/Zn13X/high_4.tiff \
  --guide data/samples/Zn13X/low_4.tiff \
  --output zn13x_fused.ome.tif \
  --backbone dinov2_vits14 \
  --fusion-method spatial_mlp \
  --upsampler cross_attn \
  --psf-profile moffat \
  --learn-psf \
  --guide-residual \
  --pore-mask auto_otsu_fringe_guarded \
  --conformal-alpha 0.10 \
  --conformal-method raps \
  --pixel-size-um 0.5

Or propagate sparse 2D chemical/diffraction slices across a 3D structural tomogram with axial interaction-volume PSF deconvolution, active next-slice beamtime steering, and OpenImpala AMReX multi-phase geometry export:

xfuse fuse-3d \
  --hr-volume xct_tomogram.h5 \
  --guide-slice 4:xrd_z04.tif 28:xrd_z28.tif \
  --output fused_3d_report.h5 \
  --pore-mask auto_otsu_fringe_guarded \
  --axial-psf-sigma 1.8 \
  --learn-axial-psf \
  --triplane \
  --suggest-next 3 \
  --export-openimpala-dir ./openimpala_geom

docs.title: Reproducible Paper Benchmarks, Ablations & LaTeX Tables
docs.text:
X-FUSE ships reproducible benchmark suites and a deterministic LaTeX table generator under benchmarks/:

# 1. Core synthetic super-resolution, contrast-to-zero failure, ECE/AUSE & 2.5D suite

  3. 03_active_acquisition_and_registration.ipynb — 3-line XFuse.fit_predict API, sub-pixel guide drift & anisotropic PSF recovery, active sparse-slice & 2D ROI steering (suggest_next_slices, suggest_2d_rois), and OME-TIFF / HDF5 report export.
